item.title: Fatou’s Lemma Intuition Revisit
item.description: Fatou’s Lemma Suppose \(\{f_n\}\) is a sequence of measurable functions with \(f_n \geq 0\). If \(\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}f_n(x) = f(x)\,\, a.e.\), then \[\int f \leq \lim \inf \int f_n\] Intuition : The RHS of Fatou’s Lemma has \(\lim \inf\) because we don’t always have \(f_n\leq f\) even though \(f_n\rightarrow f\). By the definition of the integral of non-negative function: \[\int f = \sup \int g, \,\,\text{ where } g \leq f, \text{ bounded and supported in a finite set}\]
